apg40_outcome_corrections.reason: An enabled install-check phase can silently execute no target.
Phase execution is gated by buildPlatform.canExecute hostPlatform, not cross identity alone.
A package-associated derivation owns only its exact claim and does not automatically join the package build.
Recognized flake outputs receive non-uniform validation; some are shallow or deliberately unchecked.
Substitutable checks need not execute freshly.
Effective client and daemon precedence, sandbox fallback, prerequisites, builder, and actual outcome control runtime claims.
The false-pass case includes an enabled install-check phase with no executed target.
Physical buckets are exclusive while semantic dimensions remain independently inspectable.

nix_test.scenario: A task must select which already-owned test surface proves an exact claim.
nix_test.expected: Trigger from claim, system, platform, and boundary; state what the selected surface cannot prove.

nix_test.scenario: The claim is evaluation-time well-formedness or assertion truth.
nix_test.expected: Evaluation proves no build, install, or runtime behavior.

nix_test.scenario: The claim is derivation buildability.
nix_test.expected: Build-platform evidence only; record store and log effects.

nix_test.scenario: A generic package check phase carries the claim.
nix_test.expected: It is opt-in, builder-specific, executable-platform gated, and can falsely pass when no target executes.

nix_test.scenario: A generic install-check phase carries the installed-output claim.
nix_test.expected: It is opt-in and executable-platform gated, and can silently run no tests without a custom phase, Makefile, or target.

nix_test.scenario: Check evidence is expected when build and host platforms differ.
nix_test.expected: Use buildPlatform.canExecute hostPlatform; identity inequality alone neither enables nor disables phase execution.

nix_test.scenario: A package-associated test derivation carries the claim.
nix_test.expected: Only its exact derivation claim is supported; it need not test the package and does not automatically join or change the package build.

nix_test.scenario: Uniform deep checking or building is expected for every recognized flake output.
nix_test.expected: Red overclaim; output validation is class-specific, legacyPackages is shallow, some known outputs are unchecked, and unknown outputs warn.

nix_test.scenario: Declared flake checks are relied on for selected systems.
nix_test.expected: Checks are build targets unless disabled, but substitution can satisfy buildability without fresh execution.

nix_test.scenario: No-build mode or an unselected system is presented as checked.
nix_test.expected: Make flags and systems explicit; unbuilt or unselected results cannot be represented as executed verification.

nix_test.scenario: A Nixpkgs tester or helper makes a narrow claim.
nix_test.expected: The generated surface proves only the helper's exact documented claim.

nix_test.scenario: A container test carries a service claim.
nix_test.expected: Container evidence is not virtual-machine or real-host evidence.

nix_test.scenario: A single- or multi-machine VM test carries a system claim.
nix_test.expected: Qualify topology, readiness, ordering, and bounds; never infer real-host activation.

nix_test.scenario: VM and container claims or driver layering obscure attribution.
nix_test.expected: Classify each asserted behavior by surface; Orange only for concrete obscured attribution.

nix_test.scenario: An in-profile result is described as successful activation.
nix_test.expected: Red evidence-class stop; activation is outside this profile.

nix_test.scenario: A result is described as deployment or contacts an external service.
nix_test.expected: Red evidence or authority stop absent a separately authorized bounded design.

nix_test.scenario: Sandboxing is asserted for a Linux build.
nix_test.expected: Qualify effective settings, sandbox-fallback, namespace prerequisites, derivation kind, builder, and actual outcome.

nix_test.scenario: Sandboxing is asserted for a FreeBSD build.
nix_test.expected: The exact-source default is enabled and jail-based; state it separately and note the less-exercised boundary.

nix_test.scenario: A sandbox default is asserted for another platform.
nix_test.expected: Exact 2.35.1 source defaults disabled elsewhere; claim more only from selected exact source.

nix_test.scenario: Runtime isolation is inferred from an upstream default or one configuration layer.
nix_test.expected: Record effective client and daemon precedence, trusted flake settings, sandbox-fallback, prerequisites, builder, and actual sandboxed outcome.

nix_test.scenario: A test depends on relaxed sandbox mode.
nix_test.expected: Red until exact relaxation, authority, reproducibility cost, and rollback are accepted.

nix_test.scenario: A fixed-output or chroot-opt-out derivation is involved.
nix_test.expected: Under relaxed mode it is unsandboxed; qualify every claim by derivation kind.

nix_test.scenario: Network access is claimed or required.
nix_test.expected: Qualify platform, setting, derivation kind, loopback, and external access; unqualified no-network claims are Red.

nix_test.scenario: Sandbox paths, unpinned inputs, or impurity widen visibility.
nix_test.expected: Orange until bounded and accepted; store-resident paths bring closures and reproducibility needs pinning.

nix_test.scenario: Execution uses a remote builder or emulation.
nix_test.expected: Orange until platform, trust, availability, and rollback are established; success is not local native verification.

nix_test.scenario: A binary cache or substituter can supply the result.
nix_test.expected: Yellow; supplied output is not fresh execution, and reporting it as fresh is Red.

nix_test.scenario: A platform or system matrix is declared.
nix_test.expected: Each system is a distinct target; one pass proves no other system.

nix_test.scenario: A generated mutually exclusive matrix is measured.
nix_test.expected: Use the maximum across statically exclusive arms only with execution-ownership evidence.

nix_test.scenario: The actual consumer co-schedules matrix arms.
nix_test.expected: Sum only evidenced concurrent arms and preserve differing exposure.

nix_test.scenario: Consumer behavior for package-associated tests is asserted.
nix_test.expected: Name the actual consumer and scheduling; universal claims in either direction are Red.

nix_test.scenario: A required check or install-check is skipped, empty, or executes no target.
nix_test.expected: Red false-pass stop when the test was required.

nix_test.scenario: Protected data could enter a derivation, store, log, artifact, machine, or disclosed store path.
nix_test.expected: Red protected-data stop; classify paths by what they reveal.

nix_test.scenario: An expensive test is disclosed inside an accepted capacity budget.
nix_test.expected: At least Yellow on cost; acceptable when bounded and owned.

nix_test.scenario: A large cohesive VM test has no concrete capacity risk.
nix_test.expected: Not automatically Orange; expense, size, and node count alone do not escalate.

nix_test.scenario: A concrete capacity or lifecycle risk exists.
nix_test.expected: Orange with the named risk; Red when lifecycle or resources cannot be bounded.

nix_test.scenario: One owner mixes Nix expression, driver, and phase-script material.
nix_test.expected: Assign every line to one physical bucket while inspecting semantic topology, variants, responsibilities, exposure, and coupling independently.

nix_test.scenario: Mocked behavior is compared with integrated behavior.
nix_test.expected: Disclosed mocking is Yellow; represented as integrated is Red; regenerated fixtures require semantic review.

nix_test.scenario: Stricter project policy conflicts or selection of inputs, systems, builders, caches, or commands is requested.
nix_test.expected: Stricter policy wins; selection is project-owned and is a non-trigger.

nix_test.scenario: Evaluation, build, store, container, VM, activation, deployment, or external mutation lacks authority.
nix_test.expected: Red authority stop; source review grants no execution authority.

nix_test.scenario: A claim overstates its evidence surface or ownership is too mixed to state the proven claim.
nix_test.expected: Red until decomposition or an accepted bounded exception; record reconsideration boundary.
